marco: Running through onboarding with a customer sample app and hit a teardown/body-leak with the Go generator. Pasting repro and ideas.

marco: Behavior: start generator (Iter), read a token, then call cancel on my parent ctx. After cancel we still see a goroutine stuck in a recv/send around the handshake and auth refresh; iter.Next/Close never return reliably.

marco: Minimal repro snippet: 
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
iter, err := client.Generator(ctx, req)
if err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }
_ = iter.Next()
cancel()
// expecting iter.Close/Next to unblock quickly but it can hang
```

leah: thx. Is the auth provider the default refresher? any custom token hooks?

marco: default refresher. Also using go1.22 on mac in workshop. Repro test attached in issue.

samir: quick hypothesis: auth refresher/ retry goroutine may create a derived context that isn't tied to the caller ctx, so when caller cancels the root, the refresher doesn't observe it and keeps the channel open until retry success.

leah: we've seen two related classes: (A) channel send waiting on slow consumer (backpressure) and (B) background retry goroutines not selecting on caller ctx. Both lead to "hanging" teardown.

samir: implement short-term fix: ensure every goroutine spawned by the SDK uses the passed root ctx for selects. e.g., replace `go retry(...)` with `go func(c context.Context) { select { case <-c.Done(): return } }(ctx)` and make channel sends: `select { case ch <- v: case <-ctx.Done(): return }`.

leah: DX/ergonomics follow-ups: 1) add iter.CloseWithTimeout(ctx, dur) 2) expose backpressure policy in GeneratorOptions with explicit values (Block | BufferWithTimeout | DropOldest) so sample apps can opt-in. 3) document parity with Python/Node: mention `aclose()` and `return()` analogs so onboarding docs line up.

marco: I like CloseWithTimeout + BackpressurePolicy. For onboarding, we should add a tiny quickstart snippet showing `defer func(){ _ = iter.CloseWithTimeout(context.Background(), 100*time.Millisecond) }()` and mention ForceClose semantics.

samir: agree. Also add a short integration test that simulates slow consumer and asserts no goroutine leaks within 200ms across go1.20-1.22. Tests should be flaky-tolerant but catch obvious leaks.

leah: i'll draft a small RFC for API ergonomics and update the quickstart before the next workshop. marco can you paste the goroutine dump into the GH issue?

marco: done. opened DEX-5120 "go generator cancel/teardown hang during auth retry + backpressure" and attached repro. assigned to samir.

devex-bot: Issue created: DEX-5120 "generator teardown hang during auth retry/backpressure" (assignee: samir) :white_check_mark:

marco: thanks all 1: I'll add a note to onboarding checklist so teachers tell attendees to use BackpressurePolicy=BufferWithTimeout until we ship the fix. :thumbsup:
